topIssues.title: ZKDisputeGame: a respected game can use an unrespected game as its parent
topIssues.author: Inphi
topIssues.body:
## Summary

A ZK game can start from its parent's claim. Its proof shows only that the transition from that claim is correct. `initialize()` checks that the parent did not lose, is not blacklisted or retired, has the same game type, and is above the anchor. It does not check the parent's `wasRespectedGameTypeWhenCreated`. `isGameClaimValid` checks only the child's flag.

So a claim that does not count, and that challengers may not watch, can become the start of a claim that counts.

## Where

- `packages/contracts-bedrock/src/dispute/zk/ZKDisputeGame.sol:346-368`: the parent checks.
- `packages/contracts-bedrock/src/dispute/AnchorStateRegistry.sol:331-353`: `isGameClaimValid`.

## Scenarios

1. **Rollout.** ZK is registered before it is respected. An attacker creates a ZK game with a forged root, and nobody challenges it. After ZK becomes respected, a respected child proves a correct transition from that forged root and becomes a valid claim.
2. **Incident.** A prestate bug forces a fallback to another game type. During the fallback, an attacker creates a ZK game that uses the bug. It is not retired, because it was created after the retirement time. After the switch back to ZK, a respected child of that game becomes a valid claim.

The FPVM games are not affected. They have no parents and always start from the anchor.

## Fix

Compute the child's respected flag first in `initialize()`. Then add:

```solidity
if (wasRespectedGameTypeWhenCreated && !parent.wasRespectedGameTypeWhenCreated()) revert InvalidParentGame();
```

Unrespected children can still use any parent, so proposal chains can continue after a switch away from ZK. Update the spec (`game-mechanics.md:124-126`) to match.

topIssues.title: opgeth-decoupling: own the log layer; re-home the RPC metrics hooks
topIssues.author: sebastianst
topIssues.body:
Part of #20257. See §15 of the [op-geth decoupling doc](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/develop/docs/ai/opgeth-decoupling.md). **Blocks #20266.**

## Problem

Two op-service foundation features are built on op-geth fork extensions to *general-purpose* geth
packages — nothing OP-protocol-specific, so no earlier plan section covers them, but they sit
under every service and break the whole tree at cutover:

1. **Context-based log filtering** — the fork extends `log.Logger` with `SetContext`, `WriteCtx`,
   `LogAttrs`, and `Trace/…/ErrorContext`. `op-service/log` (logfilter) builds on it;
   `op-service/testlog` implements the whole extended interface.
2. **RPC recording hooks** — the fork adds `rpc.Recorder`/`RecordedMsg`/`RecordDone`/
   `WithRecorder` inside the geth RPC client and server. `op-service/metrics` (RPC metrics),
   `op-service/rpc` (server handlers), and `op-service/client` (`WithRPCRecorder`) build on it.
   (`rpc.JsonError` in op-test-sequencer is the same family; trivially replaced by a local type.)

## Strategy

### (1) Own the log layer — `op-service/log` becomes the monorepo's logging API

Better layering regardless of the decoupling: monorepo code should depend on an internal log
layer, not on `geth/log` directly.

- **Phase 1 (now, mechanical, incremental):** add `oplog.Logger` as a *type alias* of geth
  `log.Logger`, plus re-exports of the package-level API in use (`Root`, `SetDefault`,
  `NewLogger`, level parsing, …). Sweep all monorepo imports of `go-ethereum/log` to
  `op-service/log`. Pure rename while the alias holds — landable per component, zero risk.
- **Phase 2 (at cutover):** flip the alias to an owned interface (upstream's method set + the
  context methods) with an slog-backed implementation. Implement over `slog` — do not copy
  upstream's LGPL log package; the fork's context-extension logic is OP-authored and ports over.
  Because our interface is a superset of upstream's, our loggers still satisfy upstream
  `log.Logger` wherever we hand one into geth code (e.g. the in-process L1 geth in op-e2e).

### (2) RPC recorder

- Client side: re-implement recording in our own RPC client wrappers (`op-service/client`) — we
  own that seam.
- Server side: the fork hooks observe inside geth's `rpc` server; upstream offers no equivalent.
  Needs a small design: HTTP-middleware-level observation, or wrapping the registered handlers.
  Metric continuity (names/labels) is required; per-message fidelity may be approximated.

## Acceptance criteria

- No monorepo Go file imports `go-ethereum/log` (grep is the gate).
- RPC metrics keep their metric names/labels on upstream go-ethereum; `rpc.Recorder` &
  `rpc.JsonError` uses are gone.

🤖 *Generated by Claude Code*

**Description**

The OPCM v9 upgrade tests currently build a pinned v8 development manager and stage it locally before upgrading to v9. This allows testing against forks that are still on v7, but the fixture uses the current implementation bundle rather than a finalized v8 release.

Once released v8 artifacts are available, replace the development fixture and retire the temporary setup where the normal upgrade path can provide the required starting state.

**Definition of done**

- Verify that `PastUpgrades` supplies the v8 starting state for supported fork blocks.

- Update the documentation and remove the corresponding TODOs.
- Run the full upgrade suite and ZK migration tests.

topIssues.title: op-node: write the safe-head DB once per L1 block, not per safe head
topIssues.author: sebastianst
topIssues.body:
op-node writes a safe-head DB entry with a forced disk sync ([`safedb.go#L99`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/1445c488aec5ce1fff9a5b8b7879162ee257b3cc/op-node/node/safedb/safedb.go#L99)) for every new safe head, synchronously on the driver loop ([`sync_deriver.go#L120`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/1445c488aec5ce1fff9a5b8b7879162ee257b3cc/op-node/rollup/driver/sync_deriver.go#L120)). After Holocene every derived L2 block becomes safe on its own, so an L1 block carrying K L2 blocks costs K syncs. Yet entries are keyed by L1 block number and the last write wins ([`safedb.go#L116`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/1445c488aec5ce1fff9a5b8b7879162ee257b3cc/op-node/node/safedb/safedb.go#L116)), so all but the last write per L1 block are overwritten anyway. Under disk contention each sync can take seconds, stalling the loop and RPCs that depend on it (#21952).

Proposal: write one entry per L1 block, once derivation moves past it. The forkchoice update already happens once per L1 block on the same events ([`engine_controller.go#L1100`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/1445c488aec5ce1fff9a5b8b7879162ee257b3cc/op-node/rollup/engine/engine_controller.go#L1100)). Two requirements:
- Queries must also see the not-yet-written entry. `superroot_atTimestamp` expects every block at or below local-safe to be recorded ([`superroot_api.go#L75`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/1445c488aec5ce1fff9a5b8b7879162ee257b3cc/op-node/node/superroot_api.go#L75)).
- The entry must be on disk before any forkchoice update that covers it, including finalization. Otherwise a crash leaves a gap, and `L1AtSafeHead` answers with a later L1 block.

This cuts the number of syncs but doesn't shorten each one. Removing the stall completely would also need the sync off the driver loop and a narrower lock scope, since queries wait on the same lock the write holds during the sync ([`safedb.go#L108`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/1445c488aec5ce1fff9a5b8b7879162ee257b3cc/op-node/node/safedb/safedb.go#L108), [`#L251`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/1445c488aec5ce1fff9a5b8b7879162ee257b3cc/op-node/node/safedb/safedb.go#L251)). Kona's safe-head DB isn't in use yet, so there's nothing to change there.

Related: #21953, #23111.

🤖 *Co-created with Claude Opus 5.5*

topPRs.title: Glamsterdam L1 Upgrade Compatibility
topPRs.author: max-sanchez
topPRs.body:
Sepolia activates Glamsterdam ("Amsterdam" on the execution layer) on
  2026-10-06 13:53:36 UTC. This PR keeps op-node, op-batcher and op-proposer
  working when the L1 under them forks. The L2 does not activate any Amsterdam
  feature.

  Depends on hemilabs/op-geth#111, pinned here at f5c491e251ce, which adds the
  two new L1 header fields with codecs identical to upstream v1.17.7.

  ## Changes

  - **Pin op-geth f5c491e251ce** and adapt to its API (gas-limit-aware
    `ValidateOptimismExtraData` at every call site, `SetCode`/`SetBalance`
    reasons, `ChainContext` stubs, `NewBlockChain` signature).
  - **`RPCHeader` carries `blockAccessListHash` and `slotNumber`**, so op-node's
    L1 block hash verification (and the head subscription) keeps working from
    the fork block on. Without this every post-fork block fails verification and
    derivation stops.
  - **Batcher calldata gas limit** is the larger of the old and the Amsterdam
    floor (15000 + 64 gas/byte), valid on both sides of the fork. Blob
    transactions are unaffected.
  - **Beacon spec**: read `SLOT_DURATION_MS` with a fallback to
    `SECONDS_PER_SLOT` (port of upstream #23138).
  - A guard in `RPCBlock.ExecutionPayloadEnvelope` against blocks with the new
    fields, tests for the gas-limit wiring, and fixed stale test call sites.

  Receipts, deposits, the L1 attributes deposit and the proposer were traced and
  tested and need no change.

  ## Verification
  
  - Unit tests with an upstream v1.17.7 header fixture; all 53,300 Amsterdam
    headers from execution-spec-tests through every L1 header path, 0 mismatches.
  - The op-node L1 client with full verification against the live Glamsterdam
    devnet: 472 blocks across its fork boundary, 26,071 receipts, tx types 0 to 4.
  - Every batcher transaction shape accepted by upstream v1.17.7 under Amsterdam
    rules and by Hemi's op-geth under Osaka rules.
  - Six review rounds (three on this branch, three cross-cutting).
  - The heminetwork localnet (branch `max/glamsterdam-l1-migration-e2e`) now
    forks the L1 while the stack runs, with hash verification on, in blob and
    calldata mode. It passes with this branch.

topPRs.title: ci: pilot RWX with shared routing and shadow tests
topPRs.author: teddyknox
topPRs.body:
PR validation currently rebuilds op-reth in CircleCI and lacks executed RWX parity evidence. This pilot runs the complete op-reth release producer and its three associated checks alongside shared routing, Go lint/Rust formatting, Go rollup tests and four standard-contract configurations. CircleCI continues to own the required gates.

The op-reth shadow builds both release binaries, runs every selected `reth-optimism-node` test through a nextest archive, generates fresh compact vectors with pinned develop and reads them with the PR binary, and regenerates both superchain snapshots. It uses shared dependency downloads, content caching, separate native tool caches for Cargo targets and sccache, parallel codec compilers, pinned tools and SHA-bound artifacts. Checksum-matching superchain bundles retain their timestamps. Release, integration and codec consumers mount artifacts directly instead of inheriting compiler-cache layers. Every verdict and vector generation executes freshly.

Validation:

- At `0b7935e7339726c1b1166be6372fbf057fb251dd`, [native op-reth CI](https://cloud.rwx.com/optimism/runs/0d4989f8fc044b48888ba7cdda9e9b2a) passed all four workloads in **6m20s**. All 50 runnable integration cases passed; one explicitly ignored case remained in discovery. Original JUnit identities and outcomes matched [CircleCI job 5625881](https://circleci.com/gh/ethereum-optimism/optimism/5625881) exactly. All four RWX status checks are green at this head.
- Direct artifact mounts removed both compiler-cache trees from the codec verifier. Its measured preparation fell from 171s at `99ccc76a` to 2s at this head, followed by fresh execution in 5s. The final consumer received a 622 MiB binary artifact and two small vector/provenance artifacts, and its metadata confirmed the PR checkout. Both observations are single samples, with different runner-local layer states.
- Before the bundle/artifact optimizations, the complete RWX run at `d2b90241` took 13m10s initially and [5m58s with warm tool caches](https://cloud.rwx.com/optimism/runs/2c7e09f8233541869ff6fa8771b3d372). A [forced target-cache probe](https://cloud.rwx.com/optimism/runs/8545eb684d094e13abc4e91fdab645fe) after bundle retention executed snapshot preparation in 7s, with six Rust sccache hits and zero misses; fresh regeneration still ran for 24s.
- An [empty-target probe](https://cloud.rwx.com/optimism/runs/8552f40db3314cf282583313806e0be6) produced 263 Rust hits and zero misses in 36s. An [identical-input release rerun](https://cloud.rwx.com/optimism/runs/be0b0006cd5044c88739ec46cd81f2d6) reused the compiler content cache and finished the release path in 8s, including fresh binary verification. A separate warm release rebuild recorded 27 Rust hits and no misses but still spent 236s compiling/linking; content reuse and incremental reuse have different benefits.
- An [intentional CLI-only test fault](https://cloud.rwx.com/optimism/runs/add6576e7432497a8a1e3f85a40a8313) failed the task and run, preserved nextest's exit 100, and retained original JUnit and partial coverage. Committed Rust tests were unchanged.
- 22 cache/provenance/report regression tests, 35 routing scenarios, shell checks and RWX configuration validation passed. The final native artifact consumers inherited no op-reth compiler caches; only snapshot regeneration retained Cargo targets.

Implementation coverage is **10/86 expanded PR jobs, about 12%**. The [parity checklist](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/codex/rwx-ci-pilot/docs/ai/rwx-parity-todos.md) and [measurements](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/codex/rwx-ci-pilot/docs/ai/rwx-migration.md#first-hosted-measurements) track representative Rust source-change probes, repeated actual-resource timings and billed usage, smaller tool/compiler layers, and a protected cache-rebuild policy before promotion. Whole-run duration, compiler phases and billed cost remain separate measurements; declared resource classes do not prove identical hardware. Full Go/acceptance producers and consumers, remaining Rust/contracts, routing and identity cutover remain open.

Earlier Go/contract comparisons at `587b4c3a` still need authoritative CircleCI discovery, 178 contract skip reasons and fresh evidence for 17 cached Go cases. Schedules, publishing and privileged writer ownership remain with CircleCI. The cache-only RWX vault has no production credentials and restricted pilot/develop writers; remove the temporary pilot grant and evict pilot cache entries before promotion.

This single draft PR replaces #23141, #23142, #23144 and #23148 and remains the ongoing home for the pilot.

topPRs.title: contracts-bedrock: Per-chain Review Period
topPRs.author: 0xarktos
topPRs.body:
Closes [#686](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism-private/issues/686)

## Description

Makes the withdrawal review period configurable per chain. `PROOF_MATURITY_DELAY_SECONDS` (OptimismPortal2) and `DISPUTE_GAME_FINALITY_DELAY_SECONDS` (AnchorStateRegistry) move from constructor immutables on the shared implementations to per-chain proxy storage, set at `initialize()` and changeable through an L1PAO-only setter. The implementations keep a min/max pair of constructor immutables that bound every write.

OPCM carries each chain's live value forward on upgrade. The Migrator preserves each portal's and legacy registry's value and gives the shared AnchorStateRegistry the value the legacy registries agree on. op-deployer takes the delays as per-chain inputs and the bounds as implementation inputs.

Of the ~2,000 lines added, 786 are Solidity tests, 183 are regenerated snapshots, and most of the 576 Go lines are gofmt realignment of struct literals that gained the longer bound field names. The reviewable contract change is ~460 lines.

## Design decisions

- Storage, not immutables: `proofMaturityDelaySeconds` lands in portal slot 64 and `disputeGameFinalityDelaySeconds` in registry slot 7, both tagged `@custom:network-specific`. The existing getters keep their selectors, so every reader of the delays is unaffected.

- `initialize()` and the setter share one internal `_set…` that bounds-checks, stores and emits the `…Set` event, following `SystemConfig._setGasLimit`.

- Bounds are constructor immutables with getters, standard `[1 d, 7 d]` for proof maturity and `[12 h, 3.5 d]` for the finality delay. The constructor and `DeployImplementations` reject `min == 0` and `min > max`; there is no chain-id floor in the deploy script, since VerifyOPCM checks the bound immutables at release and the StandardValidator pins the implementation.

- No `upgrade` override for the delays due to the contract size limit on the OPCM. `_loadFullConfig` reads the live getters and passes them back to `initialize()`; `overrides.cfg.proofMaturityDelaySeconds` / `…disputeGameFinalityDelaySeconds` are not allow-listed and are rejected as unknown instructions. The setters are the only write path after deployment; For atomic upgrade and delay setting batch the calls in the same superchain-ops batch.

- Due to the contract size limit, OPCM does not validate the delays and the values are checked directly on the implementation.

- It is assumed that on the time of interop migration, chains will share the same delays. The shared ASR is initialized with the finality delay every chain's registry reports, or `migrate()` reverts with `OPContractsManagerMigrator_DisputeGameFinalityDelayMismatch` before any portal is touched. The shared-registry `initialize` moved into `_initializeSharedAnchorStateRegistry` because evaluating the agreement check inline in `migrate()` hits stack-too-deep.

- `StandardValidator` gains range checks (`PORTAL-100`, `…-ANCHORP-80`): "standard" now means within the sanctioned range. `VerifyOPCM` verifies the bound immutables on the implementations (`EXPECTED_MIN_/MAX_…` env vars with standard defaults) instead of a delay value the implementation no longer holds.

- op-deployer: the delays move from `SuperchainProofParams` to `ChainProofParams` under the same JSON keys, so existing `globalDeployOverrides` keep working and per-chain `deployOverrides` can differ; the bounds take their place as implementation inputs. `op-devstack` and `op-e2e` widen the bounds for their short devnet delays.

- Versions: OptimismPortal2 6.0.0, AnchorStateRegistry 5.0.0 (constructor and `initialize` ABI change, reinit versions bumped), OPContractsManagerStandardValidator 4.1.0, OPCM V2 9.0.3 (lands in the in-development 9.x release).

## Tests

Contracts, from `packages/contracts-bedrock`:

- `just pr` — build, lint, snapshots, semver-lock, interfaces, spacers, semgrep, size check.
- `just test-dev --match-contract 'OptimismPortal2_|AnchorStateRegistry_|OPContractsManagerV2_Deploy_Test|OPContractsManagerStandardValidator_|DeployImplementations_|DeployOPChain_|VerifyOPCM_|Initializable_|SetDisputeGameImpl'` — setter and `initialize` matrix (access control, bounds, events), delay changes applied to already-proven withdrawals and already-resolved games, deploy stores the delays in proxy storage, bounds errors on deploy, rejected override keys, StandardValidator range codes, VerifyOPCM bound checks.
- `DEV_FEATURE__OPTIMISM_PORTAL_INTEROP=true just test-dev --match-contract OPContractsManagerV2_Migrate_Test` — portal and legacy-registry delays preserved, shared registry inherits the agreed value, mismatch reverts.
- `just test-dev --match-path test/invariants/OptimismPortal2.t.sol` — the ProxyAdmin owner is excluded as a sender so the fuzzer cannot move the window under the invariants.
- `just test-upgrade` (needs `ETH_RPC_URL`) — `test_upgrade_withdrawalDelaysUnchangedWithoutOverride_succeeds` proves the 7 d / 3.5 d carry-forward through the real upgrade path.

Go, from the repo root:

- `just lint-go` passes.
- `go test ./op-deployer/pkg/deployer/opcm/... ./op-deployer/pkg/deployer/pipeline/... ./op-deployer/pkg/deployer/state/... ./op-deployer/pkg/deployer/bootstrap/ ./op-chain-ops/interopgen/...` — struct mirrors load against the current script ABIs on both the script-host and forge paths, `ResolveChainProofParams` defaults and per-chain overrides, bootstrap `Check()` bound cases.
- `go test ./op-deployer/pkg/deployer/integration_test/ -run TestProofParamOverrides` — bounds verified as implementation immutables, delays verified in portal slot 64 and registry slot 7 of the deployed proxies.

## Additional context

`op-deployer bootstrap implementations` replaces `--proof-maturity-delay-seconds` and `--dispute-game-finality-delay-seconds` with `--min-/--max-proof-maturity-delay-seconds` and `--min-/--max-dispute-game-finality-delay-seconds` (env `…_MIN_/MAX_…`). Operators who set the delays through `globalDeployOverrides` are unaffected; the keys now configure the chain rather than the implementation. Chains whose live delay is outside the bounds cannot upgrade until they redeploy; every production chain is at 7 d / 3.5 d.

- [Design doc](https://app.notion.com/p/oplabs/Per-chain-airgap-and-DelayedWETH-delay-proposed-changes-and-design-3e5f153ee162809ca7ebc1cf92d1e2ab)

topPRs.title: op-node: invalidate pending gossip on unsafe-chain changes
topPRs.author: nonsense
topPRs.body:
Stacked on #22967; intentionally targets `insert-then-gossip`, not `develop`. This draft separates the correctness follow-up from optional improvements still included for review.

Queued unsafe blocks can become obsolete after local insertion. This prevents continued publication of abandoned work without putting signer/network latency back on the sequencer's hot path.

### Required for queue correctness
- **Invalidate at the authoritative head transition:** wire the publisher into `EngineController.SetUnsafeHead`; preserve unchanged heads/direct extensions and clear on rewinds, siblings, or unproven jumps. Reset requests also clear pending work. Do **not** infer reorgs from delayed forkchoice notifications: my initial implementation discarded valid blocks on delayed parent-head echoes, leaving conductor followers beyond its one-block backfill limit. That implementation is removed.
- **Make invalidation effective across concurrency boundaries:** cancel in-flight attempts without waiting for them; register cancellation/recheck queue membership under the mutex; give each enqueue its own identity so an old completion cannot remove a newly queued copy; check cancellation before pubsub handoff. Already-sent messages cannot be retracted.
- **Regression coverage:** exercise the real queue and engine head setter, delayed echoes, invalidation before notification delivery, cancellation/re-enqueue races, and preservation of slow-but-working publishes during overflow.

### Optional / independent of the correctness fix
- Serialize queue-depth metric updates; count invalidated entries and avoid reporting deliberate cancellation as a publish failure.
- Exit the publisher loop promptly when its context is canceled.
- Clarify comments: unsafe acceptance is not finality or guaranteed successful EL forkchoice adoption; publish delay excludes insertion time.
- **Draft cleanup candidate:** the additional clear on reset *confirmation* is redundant for actual reorgs now handled by the engine hook. It remains in this draft; a minimal version should remove it and revalidate the reset coverage.
- **Separate test-helper backport:** #22989 handles Raft's advisory leadership-transfer timeout by observing the actual outcome, retaining the existing settle budget and final assertions. This is already on `develop` and should be omitted when integrating onto a base that contains it.

The original PR's insert-before-publish/conductor ordering, queue capacity, timeout, retry interval, age budget, and permanent-error classification are unchanged.

Validation: full `lint-go` and `op-node` race-detector tests pass. Each of the three conductor failover/leadership-transfer acceptance tests passed **100/100** locally (op-node/op-reth, Fusaka; four shards × 25 repetitions). [Branch CI passed on the current head](https://app.circleci.com/pipelines/github/ethereum-optimism/optimism/134904).

Review performed directly using repository guidance; no independent subagent review. The optional reset-confirmation cleanup above remains open, not dismissed.
